transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... yeah, thanks. I guess I'm here because... well, I've just been getting kind of stuck on how my face looks lately. Specifically around my jaw. 

It just... it looks really sagging and uneven on one side. I didn't focus on it as much until I saw myself in a bunch of recent family photos, and now it's just hard to unsee it. My wife says she barely notices anything at all... and my clients at work don't seem to see it either, but... yeah. That's what brings me in.
How much has this concern about your jaw affected your daily life or how you feel about yourself?

I mean... I still get through my work fine. It hasn't stopped me from doing my job. I guess I've just been... maybe a little slower getting out the door when I have client meetings. And sometimes I'm probably a bit less present when I'm actually sitting with them. 

Outside of work... I don't know, I've skipped a few art openings recently. I just didn't really want to be seen, I guess... or end up in any pictures. But for the most part, I just go about my day.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking your jaw in the mirror, taking photos to examine it, or trying to fix how it looks in any way?

I guess... yeah, I do check it. Mostly before client meetings. I'll just... look in the bathroom mirror a few times. Or use my phone camera to see how it looks. Sometimes I try to fix the lighting or... maybe pull my collar up a bit, or just try to hold my head at a different angle so it's less obvious. 

And... I don't know, I guess I also find myself looking at other people a lot. Like the younger advisors at the firm, or... people at those gallery events, if I go. I just end up comparing my jaw to theirs, instead of really listening to what they're saying.
How much do these concerns about your jaw upset you emotionally, and have they ever made it hard for you to function in any part of your life, like at work or socially?

I mean... it's frustrating, I guess. But I wouldn't say I'm, you know, deeply upset or anything. It's just... annoying. 

As for work... like I said, I still do my job. It doesn't stop me from functioning. I might be a little distracted sometimes, but... I handle it. Socially... I skip a few things here and there, but it's not like I never go out. It's manageable.
Can you recall if there have been times when your concern about your jaw made it hard for you to concentrate, sleep, or enjoy things you usually like doing?

I don't think so. I sleep fine. I mean, my concentration is mostly okay, just... maybe a little off sometimes, like I mentioned before. But I still enjoy my usual things. It's not really getting in the way of all that.
Have there been times when your concern about your jaw made you feel embarrassed, ashamed, or anxious around others—even if you still managed to go out or interact with people?

I wouldn't really use those words. Um... maybe just a bit self-conscious sometimes, but... no, I wouldn't say I get anxious or ashamed. It's just... I prefer to look professional, that's all. It doesn't really get to me like that.
Have there been times when your concern about your jaw made you feel so self-conscious that it was hard to focus or feel comfortable, even in situations where you normally wouldn't have a problem?
Not really. I mean... I guess I'm always a little aware of it, but... it's not like I can't focus or get comfortable. I just... I go about my day. It's fine.
Have you ever avoided social situations or felt like you couldn't fully participate in them because you were so focused on how your jaw looks?

I mean... I still get through my work. It's fine. I guess... maybe it takes me a little longer to get out the door for client meetings lately. And... I might be a little less present during some of those appointments. Um... I have skipped a couple of art openings. Just... didn't really want to be seen, or, you know, photographed. But I wouldn't say I avoid everything.
Can you describe what goes through your mind when you're in a social situation and you're aware of how your jaw looks? Does it ever feel overwhelming or make you want to leave?

I don't know. I just... I guess I just think about if the lighting is bad, or if someone's looking at my profile. Um... it's not overwhelming. I don't run out of the room or anything. I just... wait for the meeting to be over.
Even if you don’t feel overwhelmed or anxious, do you ever feel significant distress or frustration about how your jaw looks — like it really bothers you deep down, even if you don’t show it?
I... no, not really. I don't think about it like that. It's just... I just don't like how it looks. But I wouldn't call it some deep distress or anything. It's just an annoyance, I guess.
